errors.english: because the student would have already been established previously
errors.why: rje bo is the master/owner of the property, not a student: the master would already have been established beforehand.

fix.find: because the student would have already been established previously
fix.replace: because the master would already have been established beforehand

errors.english: is itself dependent on a different specific connection
errors.why: so sor sbyor ba is the counter-correlate (pratiyogin): invariable concomitance depends on the other correlate, i.e. the probandum, which is why the probandum would be known before the sign.

errors.english: since the relationship between property and owner is not initially known, the remainder is realized later
errors.why: The Tibetan says the rest is understood even by one who does not know the property-owner relation; 'later' is not in the text and the root verse is likewise misrendered.

note: Follows the argument on the property-owner relation reasonably, but renders the master as 'the student' and blurs the counter-correlate term.

errors.english: seeing that which is without [note: seeing the nature of phenomena as being without a permanent self]
errors.why: The word completes sgrib- from the previous side: 'unobstructed' (anāvaraṇa), not 'without a permanent self'.

errors.english: seeing it as a nature that is not merely pacified, but as being empty
errors.why: Śālistamba avyupaśamasvabhāva: 'of a nature that does not cease'; 'not merely pacified, but' changes the sense and the following list is not contrasted with it.

note: A sound rendering of the Śālistamba quotation and the MMK homage verse, with a mistaken note at the opening word.

errors.english: For the followers of the (Samkhya) the Enumerators, an ancient Indian school of dualistic philosophy, the result is clarity
errors.why: ser skya continues the sage (drang srong) of the previous side: Kapila himself, for whom the seen puruṣa yields serenity, not the Sāṃkhya school.

fix.find: For the followers of the (Samkhya) the Enumerators, an ancient Indian school of dualistic philosophy, the result is clarity
fix.replace: For [the sage] Kapila, the result is clarity

errors.english: By stating "if it is accepted,"
errors.why: The lemma is 'even if one does not accept'.

fix.replace: By stating "even if it is not accepted,"

errors.english: [note: referring to the logical concomitance between the soul and its experiences]
errors.why: The root reason is the Sāṃkhya proof that objects are made of the guṇas because the guṇas (pleasure etc.) are present in them; it is not about the soul.

errors.english: Why then is the (Purusha) uncertain?
errors.why: The question is why the reason is inconclusive (anaikāntika) with respect to the puruṣa, not why the puruṣa is uncertain.

note: The anti-Sāṃkhya argument is followable, but the opening confuses Kapila with the school and a negated lemma is turned positive.

errors.english: the boundaries of the result
errors.why: The earlier rule cited is that up to completion of the result it is a single offence; 'single' is lost.

errors.english: There is no fault if a monk is made to wash items
errors.why: The offender has someone else wash the soiled items (causative); the English makes the monk the one who is made to wash.

errors.english: it concerns exchanging the (samghati) outer robe with another monk
errors.why: In this nuns' rule list the offender exchanges with a bhikṣu; 'another monk' makes the offender a monk.

note: Vinaya terms are mostly right; the offender and causative relations are blurred in a few places.

errors.english: "Come here, I am welcome."
errors.why: The forest-dweller greets the visitor: 'Come, welcome!'

note: A faithful rendering of the araṇyaka rules and the start of the miscellaneous duṣkṛtas, with one slip in the greeting.

errors.english: would it not be suspect that consciousness and the appropriating aggregates are identical?
errors.why: nye bar len pa gcig pa means having the same material cause (upādāna) as consciousness, not identity with the appropriating aggregates.

fix.find: would it not be suspect that consciousness and the appropriating aggregates are identical?
fix.replace: would it not be suspected that they share the same material cause as consciousness?

errors.english: the person does grasp the form of pleasure and so forth
errors.why: Because the puruṣa would otherwise be subject to change, it does NOT take on the form of pleasure etc.

fix.find: the person does grasp the form of pleasure and so forth
fix.replace: the person does not take on the form of pleasure and so forth

note: Generally follows the Sāṃkhya exposition but inverts a key negation and misreads the material-cause term.

errors.english: Because the nature of an action itself cannot follow
errors.why: bya nyid completes gzhal bya nyid from the previous side: knowability (prameyatva), not 'action'.

errors.english: the result of grasping the word with certainty is nothing at all
errors.why: The restrictive word ('only' in 'present only in the similar class') would have no purpose if presence in the dissimilar class were not excluded.

fix.find: the result of grasping the word with certainty is nothing at all
fix.replace: the restrictive word ("only") would serve no purpose at all

errors.english: you say: to deny both
errors.why: bshad pa introduces the author's reply that denying both is contradictory, not the opponent's statement.

errors.english: Here, the Logicians have nothing to say because
errors.why: This introduces what the Naiyāyika says (that a non-existent is neither locus nor other, so exclusion from it is impossible), which is then turned back on him; it does not say the Logicians have nothing to say.

note: The kevalānvayin debate is broadly tracked, but the restrictive-particle point and the attribution of reply and objection are garbled.

errors.english: If one thinks: 'Even if I steal this, it does not belong to a human,'
errors.why: The quoted thought is that the thing belongs to a bird, not a human; the bird is dropped.

errors.english: yet one possesses that specific perception [note: a mistaken identity of the owner]
errors.why: de'i 'du shes here is perceiving it correctly as owned by a human; the note and the run-together sentence about the five māṣakas misrepresent the condition.

note: A competent rendering of the theft subcases; one muddled passage around the five māṣakas.

errors.english: Homage to the Lotus who clearly understands through the playful manifestation of the Tathagata light rays.
errors.why: The name is Tathāgata Padmajyotirvikrīḍitābhijña: the Tathāgata who knows through the play of lotus light rays; the two elements are swapped.

fix.find: Homage to the Lotus who clearly understands through the playful manifestation of the Tathagata light rays.
fix.replace: Homage to the Tathagata who clearly understands through the playful manifestation of lotus light rays.

errors.english: because of which sentient beings are reborn in hells
errors.why: sems can dmyal ba is 'the hells'; the confessant ('I') is the one who would go there.

fix.find: because of which sentient beings are reborn in hells
fix.replace: because of which I would go to the hells

errors.english: King of the Victory Banner of Indomitable Power
errors.why: dbang po here is Indra (Indraketudhvajarāja, as the note itself says), not 'power'.

note: The Buddha-name litany and confession are mostly right; one name is scrambled and the confessant is replaced by 'sentient beings'.

errors.english: Powerful merchant families also mostly do this
errors.why: drag rigs is the kṣatriya caste: merchants and kṣatriyas also mostly do so.

fix.find: Powerful merchant families also mostly do this
fix.replace: Merchants and kṣatriyas also mostly do this

errors.english: I am afflicted
errors.why: The lemma addresses the lover: 'you are tormented'.

errors.english: one should generate aversion and think
errors.why: zhe sdang is the jealous anger the lover should feel at the scavengers ('why do you not protect it?'), not aversion toward the body.

note: The Bodhicaryāvatāra VIII glosses are mostly followed, with a caste term mistranslated and the addressee turned into 'I'.
